stories.headline: ECO Council of Ministers convenes in Islamabad for two-day regional meeting
stories.summary: Reporting on 15 November said the 30th Economic Cooperation Organization Council of Ministers meeting was due to begin in Islamabad on Sunday and continue on Monday, with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar chairing. The announcement confirms the schedule, not any negotiated outcome.
stories.background: ECO provides a regional forum for trade, connectivity and economic cooperation among its member states.
stories.what_happened: On 15 November foreign delegations arrived in Islamabad for the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting. Reported arrivals included deputy foreign ministers from Türkiye, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan and senior representatives of the SCO and OIC. Meeting outcomes were not confirmed for 15 November.
stories.why_it_matters: ECO discussions may affect cross-border trade and transport links, but announced priorities must be distinguished from binding agreements.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan is seeking stronger economic integration and transit connectivity through ECO.
key_takeaways: The 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting was scheduled for 15–16 November 2026 in Islamabad.
Ishaq Dar was announced as chair; decisions were not yet verified.
quick_gk: Islamabad was announced as host of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026.
question_angles: Who was announced as chair of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting in Islamabad?

stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition reports intercepting Houthi missiles and drones targeting Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 15 November that the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed toward Riyadh and three drones in the Eastern Province. These are coalition-reported interceptions, not independently verified damage assessments.
stories.what_happened: The coalition reported two ballistic missiles and three drones intercepted amid renewed cross-border attacks.
stories.background: Yemen's protracted conflict has repeatedly affected Saudi security and Gulf energy infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: Escalation risks for energy facilities and transport can influence global oil markets and regional security.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan is exposed to Gulf energy-market volatility and has important economic and diplomatic ties with Saudi Arabia.
stories.regional_implications: Further strikes could complicate Yemen-related de-escalation and threaten Gulf infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two ballistic missiles directed toward Riyadh and three drones in the Eastern Province.
The reported interceptions should not be conflated with confirmed impacts.
quick_gk: On 15 November 2026, the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two Houthi ballistic missiles and three drones.
question_angles: How many ballistic missiles did the Saudi-led coalition report intercepting on 15 November?

sources.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province

stories.headline: Fossil-fuel transition coalition plans continued work after Colombia's withdrawal
stories.summary: Associated Press reported on 15 November that a coalition promoting national plans to move away from fossil fuels would continue despite Colombia withdrawing. Ireland and Tuvalu are set to take over leadership, while a progress report is expected at COP31. Proposed plans are not binding climate outcomes.
stories.background: The initiative emerged from a conference in Santa Marta, Colombia, and seeks to translate broad energy-transition commitments into national road maps.
stories.what_happened: The coalition's prospective leadership transition and intended reporting were described; no new binding global treaty was announced.
stories.why_it_matters: The credibility of climate transition pledges depends on concrete implementation, financing and timelines.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Energy-importing developing countries such as Pakistan need feasible financing and grid investment for a transition.
key_takeaways: Ireland and Tuvalu were identified as incoming leaders of the voluntary fossil-fuel transition coalition.
The coalition continues despite Colombia's withdrawal.
quick_gk: Ireland and Tuvalu were identified as incoming leaders of a voluntary fossil-fuel transition coalition in November 2026.
question_angles: Which two countries were identified as incoming leaders of the fossil-fuel transition coalition?

sources.title: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion

stories.headline: Spain reports 1,488 people rescued off Canary Islands in single-day surge
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 15 November that Spain's maritime rescue service rescued 1,488 migrants from 14 boats on Saturday, 14 November, near the Canary Islands. The event occurred on 14 November and is reported here as a 15 November update, not misrepresented as a Sunday rescue.
stories.what_happened: Spanish maritime authorities reported 1,488 people rescued from 14 boats on 14 November.
stories.background: The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands involves dangerous long-distance crossings and places pressure on island reception services.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode raises questions of maritime rescue obligations, migration governance and humanitarian reception capacity.
stories.global_implications: Migration flows and rescue capacity are increasingly important issues for European and African policymakers.
key_takeaways: Spain reported rescuing 1,488 people from 14 boats on 14 November.
The report was published on 15 November; the event date was the preceding day.
quick_gk: Reuters reported on 15 November that Spain rescued 1,488 migrants from 14 boats near the Canary Islands on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: How many boats were involved in the reported 14 November Canary Islands rescue operation?

sources.title: Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Canary Islands in one day

stories.headline: Pakistan plans functional separation of sales-tax and income-tax administration
stories.summary: Dawn reported on 15 November that Pakistan's Federal Board of Revenue intends to separate sales-tax and income-tax functions within the Inland Revenue Service, reversing 17 years of functional integration. Officials estimated the sales-tax revenue gap at Rs3.4 trillion; the announced reorganization is not a creation of separate tax services.
stories.what_happened: Dedicated sales-tax commissioner-level zones are planned, with rollout at Large Taxpayer Offices beginning on 1 December 2026, followed by other offices.
stories.background: Since 2009 sales tax and income tax were jointly administered within the Inland Revenue Service. Officials say the arrangement weakened specialized sales-tax enforcement.
stories.why_it_matters: A tax collection gap undermines fiscal capacity and makes structural reform relevant to Pakistan's IMF-linked revenue objectives.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The reported sales-tax gap is an estimate of uncollected potential revenue, not an amount already collected or appropriated.
key_takeaways: The planned separation is functional and remains within the IRS.
Dawn reported an estimated Rs3.4 trillion sales-tax revenue gap.
quick_gk: Pakistan's announced 2026 FBR restructuring begins functional sales-tax separation at commissioner level, not by creating a separate tax service.
question_angles: At which administrative level will the new sales-tax functional separation begin?

sources.title: Sales tax gets new enforcement structure to cut collection gap

stories.headline: SSGC chief links restricted household gas hours to declining domestic production
stories.summary: In a 15 November interview, SSGC managing director Muhammad Amin Rajput said Pakistan's indigenous gas production had fallen about 50% over the past decade and the utility's available supply was about 605 million cubic feet per day, compared with 695 million a year earlier. The company has restricted household supply to meal-time windows.
stories.what_happened: SSGC's chief attributed constrained supply to depletion of gas fields and limited LNG availability, while describing the priority for domestic cooking periods.
stories.background: Gas shortages require allocation between households, industry, electricity generation and fertiliser production.
stories.why_it_matters: Domestic gas depletion and import exposure make energy security, storage and demand management major structural issues.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The 605 mmcfd figure is the SSGC chief's reported availability figure, not total national gas production.
key_takeaways: SSGC's chief reported about 605 mmcfd availability, down from 695 mmcfd a year earlier.
Domestic supply was prioritized around three daily meal-time windows.
quick_gk: SSGC's managing director reported gas availability of approximately 605 mmcfd in November 2026.
question_angles: What gas availability did the SSGC chief report in November 2026?

sources.title: Gas output halves in 10 years, says SSGC chief

stories.headline: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces announce withdrawal from Bab el-Mandeb area amid regional escalation
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 15 November that Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces announced a withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb area and Dhubab Airport to reinforce Aden and nearby fronts. The announcement was made against a background of Houthi advances and regional aerial attacks.
stories.what_happened: Government-aligned forces said they were redeploying from positions near the strategic strait; the report does not establish that the Houthis had captured the strait.
stories.background: Bab el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden and is strategically important to trade routes toward the Suez Canal.
stories.why_it_matters: Instability near the maritime chokepoint can raise shipping costs and risks to energy and merchandise flows.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan's importers and exporters are exposed to disruption of Red Sea routes and associated freight costs.
stories.regional_implications: The redeployment could alter military balances around Aden and shipping approaches, but its operational consequences remained uncertain.
key_takeaways: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces reported redeployment away from the Bab el-Mandeb area.
The announcement did not independently establish a change in control of the strait.
quick_gk: Bab el-Mandeb is the maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
question_angles: Which two bodies of water are linked by Bab el-Mandeb?

sources.title: Anti-Houthi forces retreat in Yemen as Iran strikes Bahrain

stories.headline: Major institutional investors warn at COP31 that climate risk threatens financial stability
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported on 15 November that representatives of 40 major pension funds, insurers and sovereign wealth funds at COP31 warned of systemic climate-related financial risks. They stressed the need for reliable public policy and investable projects, especially in emerging markets.
stories.what_happened: Institutional asset owners discussed investment risks and the barriers to financing climate projects in developing economies; no binding financial commitment by all participants was reported.
stories.background: Pension funds and insurers hold long-term assets exposed to physical climate damage and economic transition risks.
stories.why_it_matters: Climate finance depends not only on capital availability but also on credible policies, risk assessment and project structures.
stories.pakistan_perspective: For Pakistan, resilient infrastructure and transparent investment rules are important for attracting long-term climate capital.
stories.global_implications: Climate-related financial risks can affect insurers, pension funds and banks across jurisdictions.
key_takeaways: Representatives of 40 major institutional investors raised climate-financial-risk concerns at COP31.
Discussion of mobilizing finance is not equivalent to disbursement or binding commitments.
quick_gk: At COP31 in November 2026, representatives of 40 major pension funds, insurers and sovereign wealth funds discussed systemic climate-financial risks.
question_angles: Which types of institutions participated in the 40-investor climate-finance discussion at COP31?

sources.title: Pension funds raise alarm on systemic risk from climate events
